::: {.model-field-sheet}

## Purpose

This model estimates WTA player strength over time and across surfaces, with uncertainty, by treating historical market probabilities as noisy observations of latent player strength. It can derive a probability for any matchup on any surface. Current estimates are published on the [WTA Rankings](/tennis/rankings/) page.

The system has two inference stages which share the same generative model. Each off-season, the global model learns the shared parameters while integrating over the player states. During the season, those parameters remain fixed while the online player model estimates latent strengths before each day's matches.

## Data

One row per match: players $i$ and $j$, date $t$, surface $s$, player ages, prior WTA appearances, and decimal odds $o_{i,m}$ and $o_{j,m}$. The panel contains stored WTA matches from 2019 through 2025 with distinct player IDs, an unequal recorded set score, a resolved hard, clay or grass surface, both decimal prices greater than one, and a two-price overround between 0.98 and 1.20. The source distinguishes Grand Slams from other stored WTA events but does not reliably preserve lower tournament tiers.

The odds are converted to raw implied probabilities and multiplicatively de-vigged:

$$
\pi_{i,m}=\frac{1}{o_{i,m}},
\qquad
p_{i,m}=\frac{\pi_{i,m}}{\pi_{i,m}+\pi_{j,m}},
\qquad
y_m=\log\frac{p_{i,m}}{1-p_{i,m}}.
$$

The raw bookmaker margin is $v_m=\pi_{i,m}+\pi_{j,m}-1$. The model uses its training-standardized value,

$$
V_m=\frac{v_m-\bar v_{\mathrm{train}}}{s_{v,\mathrm{train}}}.
$$

The stored odds are the source's first available bookmaker; bookmaker identity is not preserved. The margin coefficient therefore describes a blend of bookmaker conventions, not a bookmaker-specific relationship between margin and noise. All standardization moments are estimated within the training panel. When forecasting a match, its own price is not used: all matches on a date are predicted before prices from that date update the player states. Match outcomes are used only for evaluation.

## States

- $x_{i,t}$ = player $i$'s overall strength at time $t$
- $\mathbf u_i=(u_{i,\mathrm{hard}},u_{i,\mathrm{clay}},u_{i,\mathrm{grass}})$ = player $i$'s surface effects
- $z$ = all player states and surface effects

## Parameters

$\operatorname{Normal}(\mu,\sigma)$ denotes a distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$; $\operatorname{Normal}_2(\boldsymbol\mu,\boldsymbol\Sigma)$ uses covariance matrix $\boldsymbol\Sigma$.

- $\theta$ = all shared system parameters
- $\tau_0$ = population entry SD, in log-odds; $\tau_0\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=1.5,\text{log-SD}=0.75)$
- $\sqrt q$ = process SD, in log-odds per square-root year; $\sqrt q\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=0.5,\text{log-SD}=1)$
- $\sqrt r$ = base observation SD, in log-odds; $\sqrt r\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=0.25,\text{log-SD}=0.75)$
- $\tau_s$ = SD of the orthonormal surface contrasts, in log-odds; $\tau_s\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=0.35,\text{log-SD}=0.75)$
- $\beta_g$ = annual pre-peak growth, in log-odds; $\beta_g\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=0.4,\text{log-SD}=0.75)$
- $\beta_d$ = annual post-peak decline, in log-odds; $\beta_d\sim\operatorname{LogNormal}(\text{median}=0.15,\text{log-SD}=1)$
- $\gamma_e$ = change in log entry SD per standardized unit of prior experience; $\gamma_e\sim\operatorname{Normal}(0,0.5)$
- $\gamma_v$ = change in log observation SD per standardized unit of bookmaker margin; $\gamma_v\sim\operatorname{Normal}(0,0.5)$

## State model

Player strength at panel entry is drawn from the tour population:

$$
\log \tau_i=\log\tau_0+\gamma_e E_i,
\qquad
x_{i,1} \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,\tau_i).
$$

$E_i$ is the training-standardized value of $\log(1+n_i)$, where $n_i$ is player $i$'s number of stored WTA appearances before entering the panel.

The live model fixes peak age at 24 and uses the piecewise-linear age path

$$
a(A;\beta)=
\begin{cases}
\beta_g(A-24), & A<24,\\
-\beta_d(A-24), & A\geq24.
\end{cases}
$$

The peak is an assumption rather than an estimated parameter. Player strength then evolves as

$$
x_{i,t} \mid x_{i,t-1}
\sim
\operatorname{Normal}\!\left(
x_{i,t-1}+a(A_{i,t};\beta)-a(A_{i,t-1};\beta),
\sqrt{q\Delta t}
\right).
$$

$\Delta t$ is elapsed calendar time in years, calculated as elapsed days divided by 365.25. The mean follows the age path; variance grows linearly with elapsed time.

Each player has two independent coordinates in an orthonormal surface-contrast basis:

$$
\mathbf c_i\sim\operatorname{Normal}_2(\mathbf 0,\tau_s^2\mathbf I_2),
\qquad
\mathbf u_i=\mathbf C\mathbf c_i,
$$

$$
\mathbf C=
\begin{pmatrix}
1/\sqrt 2 & 1/\sqrt 6\\
-1/\sqrt 2 & 1/\sqrt 6\\
0 & -2/\sqrt 6
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathbf 1^\mathsf T\mathbf u_i=0.
$$

Each named surface effect therefore has population SD $\sqrt{2/3}\,\tau_s$; effects for two different surfaces have correlation $-1/2$.

## Observation model

For match $m$, the expected market log-odds are the difference between the two players' overall strengths and surface effects:

$$
\eta_m
=
x_{i,t}-x_{j,t}+u_{i,s}-u_{j,s},
$$

Observation variance changes with bookmaker margin:

$$
\log\sqrt{r_m}=\log\sqrt r+\gamma_v V_m,
\qquad
y_m \mid z,\theta
\sim
\operatorname{Normal}(\eta_m,\sqrt{r_m}).
$$

$r_m$ determines how strongly the observed price updates the player states.

## Fit

**Off-season global fit**

Let $y_{\mathrm{train}}$ contain the eligible market log-odds from the preceding seasons in a ten-season window. The 2026 fit uses every available season from 2019 through 2025. The shared parameters are estimated by maximum a posteriori probability while the player states are integrated out:

$$
\hat\theta
=
\underset{\theta}{\arg\max}
\left\{
\log\int
p(y_{\mathrm{train}}\mid z,\theta)
p(z\mid\theta)\,dz
+\log p(\theta)
\right\}.
$$

The Gaussian integral is evaluated exactly in sparse precision form; player states are not optimizer coordinates.

**In-season online fit**

Given fitted parameters $\hat\theta$, estimate the player states from prices observed before date $t$:

$$
p(z_t\mid y_{<t},\hat\theta).
$$

Carry the state distributions forward, predict a given set of matches, then condition on the new prices. This is implemented as an information-form Kalman update.

## Results

The evaluation contains 6,381 matches from the 2024 and 2025 seasons. For each target season, the global parameters are fitted on earlier seasons and frozen; each calendar day's matches are predicted before that day's prices update the player states. The market benchmark uses the de-vigged price for the match being predicted. Standard Elo uses only outcomes observed before that day. Lower scores are better.

The Elo baseline initializes every player at 1500, uses the conventional 400-point logistic scale with a fixed $K=32$, and warms up on matches from 2021 through 2023. It maintains one rating across surfaces and is not a surface-blended Elo.

| Model | Information at prediction | Log loss | Brier |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| De-vigged market | Current match price | 0.5809 | 0.1993 |
| Player-state model | Prices before match day | 0.5973 | 0.2060 |
| Standard Elo | Results before match day | 0.6285 | 0.2198 |

The fraction of market signal retained is defined against an uninformative 50/50 forecast:

$$
S
=
\frac{\operatorname{LL}(0.5)-\operatorname{LL}(\text{model})}
{\operatorname{LL}(0.5)-\operatorname{LL}(\text{market})}.
$$

| Surface | Matches | Model log loss | Market | Elo | Signal retained |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Hard | 3,951 | 0.6005 | 0.5864 | 0.6330 | 86.8% |
| Clay | 1,663 | 0.5794 | 0.5608 | 0.6167 | 86.0% |
| Grass | 767 | 0.6196 | 0.5964 | 0.6304 | 76.1% |
| **Overall** | **6,381** | **0.5973** | **0.5809** | **0.6285** | **85.4%** |

The model recovers 65.6% of the log-loss gap between standard Elo and the current-match market. Performance is weakest on grass, where the evaluation sample is smallest.

## Validation

Paired log-loss differences were resampled by calendar day, preserving the dependence among matches played on the same day.

| Comparison | Difference | Day-clustered 95% interval |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Model − Elo | −0.0312 | [−0.0376, −0.0245] |
| Model − market | +0.0163 | [+0.0117, +0.0207] |

Outcome calibration is estimated by regressing the observed result on the model log-odds. An intercept of zero and slope of one indicate calibration. Pooled across both seasons, the intercept is −0.008 [−0.065, 0.045] and the slope is 1.045 [0.982, 1.116]. The slopes are 1.087 [0.996, 1.178] in 2024 and 1.007 [0.912, 1.110] in 2025.

| Surface | Matches | Intercept [95% interval] | Slope [95% interval] |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Hard | 3,951 | −0.016 [−0.083, 0.054] | 1.019 [0.929, 1.109] |
| Clay | 1,663 | +0.021 [−0.079, 0.122] | 1.182 [1.048, 1.340] |
| Grass | 767 | −0.019 [−0.178, 0.144] | 0.909 [0.748, 1.069] |

The predictive distribution for a market price combines uncertainty in the latent matchup with fitted observation noise. If that distribution is calibrated, its standardized innovations have SD one and its central intervals attain their nominal coverage.

| Surface | Innovation SD | 50% interval | 80% interval | 95% interval |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Hard | 0.953 | 53.0% | 83.4% | 96.3% |
| Clay | 0.976 | 52.1% | 81.5% | 95.6% |
| Grass | 1.121 | 48.1% | 77.4% | 91.9% |
| **Overall** | **0.981** | **52.2%** | **82.2%** | **95.6%** |

The overall predictive intervals are slightly conservative, while the smaller grass sample is under-dispersed.

Latent-state uncertainty was checked against later revisions. For each audit point, let $(m_f,P_f)$ be the pre-match filtered mean and variance, and $(m_s,P_s)$ the estimate of the same state after prices through 2025 are allowed to smooth it. Under the fitted state model,

$$
z=\frac{m_s-m_f}{\sqrt{P_f-P_s}}
\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,1).
$$

The player-state sample takes one appearance per player-month in 2024. Intervals for those rows are clustered by player; matchup-contrast intervals are clustered by match date.

| Quantity | Observations | Mean revision [95% interval] | Revision SD [95% interval] | 95% coverage |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Overall player state | 1,990 | −0.207 [−0.256, −0.158] | 0.963 [0.921, 1.005] | 95.3% |
| Played-surface player state | 1,990 | −0.186 [−0.233, −0.139] | 0.991 [0.950, 1.035] | 94.4% |
| Matchup contrast | 3,167 | +0.003 [−0.034, 0.041] | 1.035 [1.007, 1.064] | 94.5% |

The player-state interval widths are approximately calibrated to later market information. Their absolute levels revise downward together, but this shift disappears from the identifiable player-versus-player contrast. Matchup uncertainty is slightly narrow overall and most clearly so on grass, where its revision SD is 1.09. These are statements about later market beliefs, not independently observed true skill. The [player-state revisions](/assets/data/wta-state-revision-audit.csv), [matchup revisions](/assets/data/wta-matchup-revision-audit.csv) and [audit script](https://github.com/spazznolo/spazznolo.github.io/blob/master/scripts/wta_state_revision_audit.py) reproduce the check.

Successive signed market innovations for the same player remain correlated at short intervals:

| Consecutive appearances | Pairs | Correlation |
|:--|--:|--:|
| 1–7 days, same tournament | 6,165 | 0.116 |
| 1–7 days, different tournament | 1,477 | 0.199 |
| 8–30 days | 3,145 | 0.096 |
| More than 30 days | 1,156 | 0.005 |

The one-to-seven-day estimate is 0.130 [0.104, 0.156], compared with 0.005 [−0.084, 0.090] after more than 30 days. Dependence is not concentrated within tournaments, so a missing tournament intercept cannot explain the pattern by itself. Prices contain slowly varying information—potentially form, health or market memory—that the observation model does not represent.

Peak age was tested by refitting the complete system at four fixed values. Differences are relative to peak 24 and use the same day-clustered bootstrap as the benchmark comparison.

| Fixed peak | Log loss | Difference [95% interval] |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 22 | 0.59781 | +0.00054 [+0.00003, +0.00105] |
| 24 | 0.59727 | 0 |
| 26 | 0.59718 | −0.00009 [−0.00049, +0.00030] |
| 28 | 0.59710 | −0.00017 [−0.00077, +0.00039] |

Next-match performance does not distinguish peaks from 24 through 28. That is expected: most appearances are close together, age drift is small over the forecast interval, and each new price updates the state again. The stable log loss is not evidence that the aging curve is correct. Age 24 remains an external interpretive constraint rather than a data-identified biological peak. A proper test must freeze player states and score one- to three-year projections without intermediate market updates. The [sensitivity data](/assets/data/wta-peak-sensitivity.csv) and [script](https://github.com/spazznolo/spazznolo.github.io/blob/master/scripts/wta_peak_sensitivity.py) reproduce the short-horizon comparison.

The [evaluation data](/assets/data/wta-model-validation.csv) and [validation script](https://github.com/spazznolo/spazznolo.github.io/blob/master/scripts/wta_validation.py) reproduce these diagnostics.

## Output

The model supplies player-level strengths, surface effects, historical trajectories, matchup probabilities, and uncertainty. These are available as [weekly rankings](/tennis/rankings/).
